i.norm: Verifies that parseFromCentralDirectoryData throws ArrayIndexOutOfBoundsException when the flags byte has CREATE_TIME_BIT (0x04) set but the buffer does not contain enough bytes after the flags byte to read the required 4-byte timestamp value. Buffer layout: [0x00, 0x00, 0x04] (length 3) - offset 2 points to the flags byte (value 0x04 = CREATE_TIME_BIT set) - after consuming the flags byte the read position moves to index 3, which is past the end of the 3-element array, causing ByteUtils to throw ArrayIndexOutOfBoundsException when it tries to read 4 bytes.
Three-byte buffer where only index 2 (the flags byte) is populated. Setting it to CREATE_TIME_BIT (4) tells the parser that a 4-byte create-timestamp follows, but no such bytes exist in the buffer.
Parse starting at offset 2 with a large declared length (25461), so the length check inside the parser does not guard against the missing timestamp bytes — only the physical array boundary does.
ByteUtils tries to read from index 3 of a length-3 array
